details:
Our project, Abandoned but Not Forgotten, is an interactive space exploration website that helps people discover the story of NASA's spacecraft, rovers, landers and scientific instruments that were left behind on the Moon, Mars and in deep space.

The website works like a digital space museum where visitors can explore different destinations, discover historical space equipment, view real NASA photographs, learn about their missions and understand the scientific discoveries they made. We are also incorporating an interactive mission timeline, 3D spacecraft models, a mission control simulation and quizzes to make the experience more engaging, specially for school students.

The main benefit of this project is that it makes space science easier to understand and more interesting. Instead of only reading long technical information, users can interact with the content and learn through visual storytelling. Our aim is to create curiosity among students and help them understand how these missions contributed to our knowledge of the universe.

We are developing the website using HTML, CSS and Vanilla JavaScript, along with public NASA resources and its Image and Video Library API. We are also using browser technologies like LocalStorage, SVG and Canvas for interactive features. No backend or separate database is required.

What makes our project creative is the idea of presenting forgotten space hardware as an interactive museum, giving every machine its own story. While developing it, we considered scientific accuracy, ease of use, mobile responsiveness, accessibility, visual quality and making the experience suitable for students. Our belief is that even when a mission ends, its contribution to science should never be forgotten.
